stories.headline: Lupin beat Q1 targets but cut FY27 US revenue guidance to $1.1-1.2B from 'billion-plus'
stories.instagram_caption:
Lupin's Q1 FY27 revenue grew 32% YoY with 30% EBITDA margins, beating expectations.
Management revised its FY27 US business guidance to $1.1-1.2B, down from the prior 'billion-plus, sustained' framing, citing new generic competition on Tolvaptan (Apotex, Teva) and pricing pressure on Mirabegron from Q2.
Full-year EBITDA margin guidance was maintained at 25%.
Ex-US business grew over 20% across India, Europe and emerging markets.
Factual summary of public company disclosures. Not investment advice.
stories.youtube_shorts_script:
[ON-SCREEN: LUPIN — Q1 FY27]
Lupin's Q1 revenue grew 32% year-on-year, with EBITDA margins at 30% — a beat versus expectations.
[ON-SCREEN: US GUIDANCE: 'billion-plus' -> $1.1-1.2B]
But management revised its FY27 US business guidance down to $1.1 to $1.2 billion, from the prior framing of sustaining 'billion-plus' revenue.
[ON-SCREEN: WHY: Tolvaptan & Mirabegron competition]
The company cited new generic competition on Tolvaptan from Apotex and Teva, plus pricing pressure on Mirabegron starting Q2.
[ON-SCREEN: FULL-YEAR MARGIN GUIDANCE: 25%, unchanged]
Full-year EBITDA margin guidance stayed at 25%, and ex-US markets grew over 20%.
Factual summary of public company disclosures. Not investment advice.

stories.headline: Varroc raised FY27 growth guidance to 20-25%, while flagging underlying organic growth of just 4%
stories.instagram_caption:
Varroc Engineering raised its FY27 growth guidance to 20-25%, up from the prior mid-to-high teens range.
The revision follows a 29.9% nominal revenue beat in Q1 - but management noted underlying organic growth, excluding inflation pass-through, was only about 4%.
EBITDA margin came in at 8.5%, down from 9.4% a year earlier, on one-time war-related and tooling costs described as recoverable.
Factual summary of public company disclosures. Not investment advice.
stories.youtube_shorts_script:
[ON-SCREEN: VARROC — Q1 FY27]
Varroc Engineering's Q1 revenue grew 29.9% year-on-year in nominal terms.
[ON-SCREEN: FY27 GUIDANCE: mid-to-high teens -> 20-25%]
On the back of that, management raised its full-year FY27 growth guidance to 20 to 25%, up from a prior mid-to-high-teens range.
[ON-SCREEN: BUT: organic growth ~4%]
But management also disclosed that underlying organic growth - stripping out inflation-linked pass-through pricing - was only around 4%.
[ON-SCREEN: EBITDA MARGIN: 8.5% vs 9.4% prior year]
EBITDA margin came in at 8.5%, versus 9.4% a year earlier, which management attributed to one-time war-related and tooling costs.
Factual summary of public company disclosures. Not investment advice.

stories.headline: Bajaj Electricals targeted 8-10% quarterly growth, delivered 2.3%
stories.instagram_caption:
Bajaj Electricals had targeted 8-10% quarterly revenue growth for Q1.
Actual growth came in at 2.3%, missing that range.
Consumer Products grew just 1.7% versus an expected stronger bounce-back; Lighting Solutions grew 4.4%.
EBIT margin improved to 6.6% from 2.5% a year earlier, tracking the company's 6-7% near-term margin guidance.
Factual summary of public company disclosures. Not investment advice.
stories.youtube_shorts_script:
[ON-SCREEN: BAJAJ ELECTRICALS — Q1 FY27]
Bajaj Electricals had targeted 8 to 10% quarterly revenue growth for this quarter.
[ON-SCREEN: TARGET 8-10% vs ACTUAL 2.3%]
Actual revenue growth came in at just 2.3%, well below that range.
[ON-SCREEN: Consumer Products +1.7%, Lighting +4.4%]
Consumer Products, which management expected to bounce back, grew only 1.7%. Lighting Solutions grew 4.4%.
[ON-SCREEN: EBIT MARGIN: 6.6% vs 2.5% last year]
On the positive side, EBIT margin improved to 6.6% from 2.5% a year earlier, in line with the company's 6-7% near-term margin guidance.
Factual summary of public company disclosures. Not investment advice.

stories.headline: IRM Energy's Q1 EBITDA/SCM hit INR10, above its prior guided INR5-6 range
stories.instagram_caption:
IRM Energy had previously guided EBITDA per SCM in the INR 5-6 range.
Q1 FY27 EBITDA/SCM came in at INR 10, substantially ahead of that guidance.
Management attributed this to favourable sourcing this quarter and guided the next three quarters lower, at INR 7-8/SCM.
Revenue grew 24% YoY to INR 326 crore; volumes grew 8% YoY, on track for the full-year 10-12% growth target.
Factual summary of public company disclosures. Not investment advice.
stories.youtube_shorts_script:
[ON-SCREEN: IRM ENERGY — Q1 FY27]
IRM Energy had previously guided EBITDA per SCM of gas sold in the range of 5 to 6 rupees.
[ON-SCREEN: GUIDED INR5-6 vs ACTUAL INR10]
Q1 actual EBITDA per SCM came in at 10 rupees, well above that guided range.
[ON-SCREEN: WHY: favourable sourcing this quarter]
Management said this was driven by favourable gas sourcing this quarter, and guided the next three quarters lower, at 7 to 8 rupees per SCM.
[ON-SCREEN: REVENUE +24% YoY, VOLUME +8% YoY]
Revenue grew 24% year-on-year to 326 crore rupees, with volumes up 8%, on track for the full-year 10 to 12% growth target.
Factual summary of public company disclosures. Not investment advice.

stories.company_name: Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertilizers and Chemicals Limited
stories.headline: GNFC posted its second-highest quarterly profit ever but declined to give Q2 guidance
stories.instagram_caption:
GNFC reported its second-highest quarterly profit in company history this quarter.
Its fertiliser segment recovered sharply to INR 85 crore, reversing the pessimism management had flagged back in May.
Despite the strong quarter, management declined to give Q2 guidance, citing ongoing volatility.
Cost-saving initiatives worth INR 250-300 crore (with A.T. Kearney) are progressing, with impact still pending.
Factual summary of public company disclosures. Not investment advice.
stories.youtube_shorts_script:
[ON-SCREEN: GNFC — Q1 FY27]
GNFC posted its second-highest quarterly profit in the company's history this quarter.
[ON-SCREEN: Fertiliser segment: INR85cr, reversing May pessimism]
Its fertiliser segment recovered sharply to 85 crore rupees, a reversal from the cautious tone management struck back in May.
[ON-SCREEN: Q2 guidance: not given]
Despite that, when asked, management declined to give Q2 guidance, citing ongoing volatility.
[ON-SCREEN: Cost savings target: INR250-300cr, pending]
A cost-saving programme with A.T. Kearney, targeting 250 to 300 crore rupees, is still progressing, with its impact yet to show up in results.
